summary: OpenAI published an internal economic-research report showing how usage of its Codex agent tool grew across departments and user types over the past year, measured in tokens, task duration, and adoption rates.

mechanisms.reason: The document reports that Codex now accounts for almost all of OpenAI's internal output tokens and describes rapid multi-fold growth in usage across user groups.
mechanisms.quote: Codex accounts for 99.8% of weekly output tokens generated within OpenAI.

mechanisms.reason: The report documents a shift from short chatbot interactions to long-horizon, parallel agent execution across an entire organization, including non-technical departments.
mechanisms.quote: By June 2026, users at the 99th percentile regularly generated more than 60 hours of Codex agent turns per day, distributed across multiple, parallel agents.

practices.reason: The paper's method of estimating task horizon via LLM-as-judge over agent transcripts is a measurement approach a team could adapt to gauge agentic task complexity, though it is described only generically.
practices.quote: Task horizon is estimated using an LLM-as-judge with access to Codex transcripts.

notable_reason: It gives concrete, lab-measured figures on how far and how fast agentic usage has displaced chatbot interactions inside a frontier lab, a rare quantified look at the agentic-workflow shift.
